newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australians warned of Indonesia travel risk.
newsitem.headline: Australians warned of Indonesia travel risk.

text.p: Australians were advised on Thursday of the dangers of travel in Indonesia because of pre-election violence and told that if they did visit the Southeast Asian archipelago they should avoid crowds.
Australia's foreign affairs department warned Australians that they should be alert to possible violent disturbances in Jakarta and other cities leading up to the May 29 election.

"In particular, they should avoid any crowds or becoming caught in political disturbances," the department said in a statement. Embassies in Jakarta had already warned foreign residents to stay indoors.

The ruling Golkar party is widely expected to win the election and most of the violence during the campaign has involved clashes between the supporters of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and Golkar suppporters.
